title: Debug an Unreachable Web App
description:
## Debug an Unreachable Web App

A web application has been deployed to the `webshop` namespace, but it is completely unreachable through its Service. The platform team reports that the Service `web` returns no endpoints and the pods never become Ready.

**There is more than one thing wrong.** You must find and fix every fault so that:

- the `web` Deployment has **all 3 pods in Ready state**, and
- the `web` Service has **live endpoints** backing it.

```bash
# Start your investigation:
kubectl get all -n webshop
kubectl describe deployment web -n webshop
kubectl describe pod -n webshop -l app=web
kubectl get endpoints web -n webshop
```

> 💡 Work layer by layer: are the pods Ready? If not, why? Then — does the Service actually select the pods, and does it target the right container port?

hints.title: Why are the pods not Ready?
hints.body: Describe a pod and read the Events and the readiness probe section. The readiness probe is checking an HTTP path that the nginx image does not serve, so the probe never succeeds and the pod stays un-Ready. Point the probe at a path that returns 200 (the nginx root path).
hints.command: kubectl describe pod -n webshop -l app=web | grep -A15 'Readiness\|Events'

hints.title: Fix the readiness probe path
hints.body: Patch the deployment so the readiness probe uses the root path '/' instead of the missing '/healthz' endpoint.

hints.title: Why does the Service have no endpoints?
hints.body: Compare the Service spec against the pods. The Service targetPort points at a port the container does not expose. The pods serve on container port 80, but the Service forwards traffic to the wrong targetPort, so even Ready pods are never registered as usable endpoints.
hints.command: kubectl get svc web -n webshop -o jsonpath='{.spec.ports}' && echo && kubectl get pod -n webshop -l app=web -o jsonpath='{.items[0].spec.containers[0].ports}'

hints.title: Fix the Service targetPort
hints.body: Patch the Service so its targetPort matches the container port 80.

setup_commands.command:
kubectl apply -n webshop -f - <<EOF
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: Deployment
metadata:
  name: web
  labels:
    app: web
spec:
  replicas: 3
  selector:
    matchLabels:
      app: web
  template:
    metadata:
      labels:
        app: web
    spec:
      containers:
      - name: nginx
        image: nginx:1.25
        ports:
        - containerPort: 80
        readinessProbe:
          httpGet:
            path: /healthz
            port: 80
          initialDelaySeconds: 2
          periodSeconds: 3
EOF

kubectl apply -n webshop -f - <<EOF
apiVersion: v1
kind: Service
metadata:
  name: web
spec:
  selector:
    app: web
  ports:
  - port: 80
    targetPort: 8080
EOF

validation.description: Checks that the web deployment is fully Ready and the Service has live endpoints.

commands.command: kubectl get deployment web -n webshop -o jsonpath='{.status.readyReplicas}' 2>/dev/null | grep -v '^$' || echo 0

commands.description: Service 'web' targetPort points at container port 80
commands.command: kubectl get svc web -n webshop -o jsonpath='{.spec.ports[0].targetPort}'

commands.description: Service 'web' has at least one live endpoint address
commands.command: kubectl get endpoints web -n webshop -o jsonpath='{.subsets[0].addresses[0].ip}' 2>/dev/null | grep -v '^$' || echo empty
